correctness.rationale: Normalized affine interpolation traces the shorter great-circle arc; its planar projection has the argument of a positive combination of two nonopposite endpoint rays and sweeps the entire shorter azimuthal arc. Uniform conditioned azimuths put mass ell/theta on each component. Different components cannot connect inside E. In a lift of one component to (0,ell), the excluded pairs are the two triangular corners with |U−V|>pi, of total area (ell−pi)_+². This applies when ell=2pi with a single omitted angle as well. Axis and antipodal cases do not contribute; equal or opposite angular pairs have zero probability under independent uniform azimuths. With f(s)=s²−(s−pi)_+², the supporting line at theta/k touches only there (also when theta/k=pi), giving the stated unique lower equality case; strict increase of f(s)/s proves strict superadditivity on positive arguments. One arc tending to theta with the others shrinking proves sharpness, even for theta=2pi with singleton cuts.

value.rationale: For a natural class of spherical domains the exact geometry reduces to a length distribution and yields a sharp design law: equal components minimize containment, and concentration of length approaches an unattained supremum. The law captures the failure of area alone to control geodesic containment, including null-area cuts, and works without polar-coordinate information beyond the uniform azimuthal marginal.
